a) the diagnosis of renal carcinoid is often missed in the presence of metastases, and b) the diagnosis of primary renal carcinoid is difficult, and may be misdiagnosed in the presence of a metastatic RCC, especially if the metastasis is cutaneous.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the diagnosis of RCC is often difficult, particularly when the histopathology shows a papillary growth pattern, as in the case described here, and the diagnosis of carcinoid is even more challenging, especially when the tumour is located in a non-classical site such as the kidney.
the primary renal carcinoid was misdiagnosed and the patient had undergone unnecessary treatment with sorafenib.

this case illustrates the importance of a thorough histological review, especially in cases of renal tumours with unusual features, to avoid the misdiagnosis of a metastatic renal cell carcinoid tumour, which is a rare entity with a different prognosis and treatment from that of renal cell carcinoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a renal carcinoid should be considered in the differential diagnosis of renal cell carcinoma, especially in patients with metastatic disease.
a carcinoid tumour should be considered in the differential diagnosis for pulmonary nodules that are discovered in patients with a history of RCC, even after several years.
carcinoid tumours can be difficult to differentiate from RCC.
